column2: A superacid of fluorosulfuric acid and antimony pentafluoride, vastly stronger than sulfuric acid. It got its name in George Olah's lab in 1966, when a colleague dropped a piece of Christmas candle into it and the wax dissolved.
Made from hydrogen fluoride and antimony pentafluoride, and often called the strongest acid there is. It's a favourite of science videos, which is why so many people know the name.
